Where Hirsel trails Rust

Headline geomeans hide real gaps. These are the largest rows where Hirsel is slower or uses more memory than the Rust peer on this board run:

LangArena / Json::Generate

2.05× seconds · 2.50× instructions vs Rust

Largest runtime loss on the board; Hirsel JSON serialization does roughly twice the work of the Rust port.

LangArena / Etc::LogParser

1.31× seconds · 1.73× instructions vs Rust

Regex/log-parsing hot loop executes 73% more instructions and 31% more wall time than Rust.

Compile instructions (LangArena)

1.55× cold · 1.20× warm edit (1.36× geomean)

While warm edit wall time is 0.91× Rust, cold compile wall time is 1.13× and total compiler instructions remain higher on both.

Checkbox server (64 clients)

0.82× throughput (lower) · 2.24× unsubscribed RSS

Hirsel delivers 82% of Rust throughput (7,162 vs 8,766 toggles/s) and uses 2.24× Rust RSS for unsubscribed sessions (196 vs 87 KiB/session), though subscribed RSS is 0.75× Rust.

Methodology & caveats

Checks kept on

Hirsel keeps bounds checks, integer overflow checks, logical byte admission, and step charges (wherever a step bound can be current) enabled. The Rust and Goose peers check bounds only.

Runtime instruction counts measure user-space CPU work with all PMU counters 100% active. Seconds use perf duration_time around the whole process (startup, setup, warmups, measured iterations, verification, exit).

Every seconds row is a single sample per side: no repeats, so no minimum, maximum or spread is published for it. The instruction counts are the measurement the nightly gate checks.

Bench host

This board run predates host recording, so its CPU model, kernel, governor, boost and SMT state are not published.

Compiler build (no BOLT)

The nightly board builds the Hirsel compiler with DIST_BOLT=off, so its Compile rows measure a compiler without BOLT. Shipped releases are built with --bolt: the compiler is BOLT-optimized on a profile from the release std and cold LangArena builds, the same LangArena workload the Compile rows use. The board never measures that release binary.

Libraries, layouts & verification

The ports use different libraries and data layouts; ratios compare full implementations rather than identical IR. LangArena runs the pinned upstream run.js fixture with upstream checksums, and each AWFY row verifies its reference result internally.

Compile rows keep dependencies built, use one Cargo codegen unit with release incremental enabled, and edit Spectralnorm’s checksum for the warm rebuild. Checkbox RSS subtracts the server’s startup/idle reading before sessions open from the reading with 64 live sessions, then divides only that increase by 64.

Matmul threading notes

  • LangArena/Matmul::T4: Hirsel submits 4 row blocks to one worker for the process run. Rust creates and drops a 4-worker Rayon pool each iteration. Goose starts 4 workers at construction and joins them at checksum time. All workers share the measurement CPU.
  • LangArena/Matmul::T8: Hirsel submits 8 row blocks to one worker for the process run. Rust creates and drops an 8-worker Rayon pool each iteration. Goose starts 8 workers at construction and joins them at checksum time. All workers share the measurement CPU.
  • LangArena/Matmul::T16: Hirsel submits 16 row blocks to one worker for the process run. Rust creates and drops a 16-worker Rayon pool each iteration. Goose starts 16 workers at construction and joins them at checksum time. All workers share the measurement CPU.
